detailed_description: The Character Frequency Analyzer performs granular statistical analysis of textual input by calculating the occurrence distribution of Unicode characters, glyphs, and byte values. This tool leverages UTF-8 encoding validation, case-insensitive comparison flags, and customizable whitespace handling to generate multi-dimensional frequency metrics. Developers and researchers use this tool for cryptanalysis of classical ciphers, linguistic pattern recognition, data quality assessment, and algorithm optimization. It processes input through a three-stage pipeline: first normalizing text using Unicode Normalization Form C, then constructing a hash table mapping character code points to counters, and finally applying entropy calculation algorithms to determine distribution patterns. The output includes raw counts, percentage weights, and visual heatmaps that highlight statistical outliers in the character distribution.
usage_steps: Paste UTF-8 encoded text into the resizable input textarea or drag-and-drop a .txt/.csv file
Toggle 'Case-Sensitive Mode' to differentiate uppercase/lowercase characters
Select 'Whitespace Handling' options: include/exclude spaces, tabs, newlines, or Unicode whitespace
Click 'Analyze' to initiate the multi-threaded processing engine
Review interactive histogram showing frequency distribution and entropy metrics
Export results via JSON download or copy-paste the tab-separated values table
usage_examples: Cryptographers analyzing Vigenère cipher outputs to detect key length patterns through periodic frequency spikes
Linguists comparing vowel consonant ratios across different language corpora for phonetic research
Data engineers validating JSON log files by checking for anomalous ASCII control character frequencies
Game developers optimizing text rendering performance by identifying most-used glyphs in UI strings
